clue.text: Live with drunkard holding record that could be 18

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: the drunkard's word holds the record inside it

parts.note: a lush is a heavy drinker
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A drinking companion clutches a favourite record, which apparently could be thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is the theme answer, ELECTRIC: many clues define their answer only as something that can take that word in front of it. 'holding' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorbell button is typically wired up, so it is an example of something powered by current.

clue.text: Sack could be 18

definitions.meaning: to sack is to dismiss from a job
a room heater burning or glowing, which may be powered by mains current

explanation.definitionFit: Dismissing an employee is a synonym, and a household heating appliance can run on mains power.

clue.text: … confused with a 2, could be 18

definitions.meaning: 2 refers to the answer at 2-down; a room-warming appliance is easily confused with that
a room-warming appliance that may be run on mains current

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the clue to 2-down; the first definition says this appliance is often taken for that one.
explanation.definitionFit: A heating appliance is near enough to a gas or bar fire to be confused with it, and many run on mains current.

clue.text: Acquire note with points that could be 18

parts.note: to win something is to acquire it
DO is a note of the sol-fa scale
W, west, is a compass point
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Gain a musical note together with some compass directions, all of which might be thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Car windows that go up and down at the press of a button are a standard example of powered fittings.

clue.text: It's socially unacceptable and demands hard work

definitions.text: It's socially unacceptable and demands hard work

parts.words: It's socially unacceptable and demands hard work
parts.note: a pun on infra dig, socially beneath one: heavy earth that is hard to dig through demands a great deal of spadework

explanation.walkthrough: Infra dig means beneath one's dignity, socially unacceptable; the joke reads it as 'hard to dig', which describes heavy, sticky garden ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy sticky earth is notoriously hard to dig, which the clue renders as being infra dig.

clue.text: Emphasise name for lingerie

parts.note: to emphasise words is to underline them

explanation.surface: Advice to stress the label given to ladies' underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Underclothes, especially women's delicate ones, were once called by this name for the fabric they were made of.

clue.text: Accusation could be 18

definitions.meaning: a formal accusation of a crime
a quantity held by a battery or a body carrying current

explanation.definitionFit: An indictment is a synonym, and in physics the term means a store of electric energy.

clue.text: Report of a couple of fruits producing disease

indicators.note: report means what is heard, so the letters sound like the clue words said aloud

parts.note: two berries, berry berry

explanation.surface: Eating two pieces of fruit is reported to have made someone ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A vitamin B1 deficiency illness common where diets are of polished rice.

clue.text: Left local man at loch

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub, an inn
a man is a he

explanation.surface: A local man departed and went off to a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is not an adjective here: in Britain your local is your nearest pub. Loch Linnhe is a sea loch in the west of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A long sea inlet in the Scottish Highlands near Fort William.

clue.text: Athletic distinction could be 18

definitions.meaning: at Oxford and Cambridge a sportsman who represents the university is awarded this colour
a vivid steely shade of that colour is called by the theme word

explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge universities a student who represents the university against the other in a sport wins a 'Blue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Representing Oxford or Cambridge earns a sporting colour, and a brilliant shade of that colour has the theme's name.

clue.text: Single piece of 6 supports picnickers

parts.note: 6 refers to the answer at 6-down, lingerie; a one-piece item of it is a teddy
to support is to bear

explanation.surface: One garment from the lingerie drawer holds up some people eating outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the song 'The Teddy Bears' Picnic'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the well-known children's song the toy animals go to the woods for a picnic.

clue.text: Sailor following some guidance could be 18

indicators.note: the sailor comes after the part of guidance
only some of the word guidance, its opening letters, is used

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman taking some advice might turn out to be thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock musician's instrument is often amplified and plugged in, a familiar case of a powered instrument.

clue.text: Bird, hiding its head as well to start with, could be 18

indicators.note: the word for as well is placed at the start

parts.note: as well means too

indicators.note: the bird conceals a letter within it

parts.note: a thrush is a songbird
the head of the word bird, its first letter

explanation.surface: A songbird keeps its head down, and as well as that might be thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its head' means the first letter of 'Bird', which 'hiding' tucks inside the bird's name; 'to start with' signals that the word for 'as well' leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Battery-powered brushes for cleaning teeth are a common household example of a powered gadget.

clue.text: Kingfisher's familiar garments?

definitions.meaning: Kingfisher plc once owned Woolworths, whose familiar nickname this is

explanation.walkthrough: Kingfisher is not the bird but the British retail group that once owned Woolworths, a chain store known affectionately by this nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet name for the Woolworths chain store, and also an informal term for warm knitted clothes.

clue.text: A toy used at tea time said to make one hoarse

parts.note: tea is spelt as the letter T
HR, hour, is a unit of time

indicators.note: used means worked over, so the letters of a toy are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of a toy

explanation.surface: A child's plaything brought out at teatime is said to make someone's voice rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' signals the anagram of A TOY. 'at' only joins the pieces, which are set down tea and time first.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, deep voice that seems to come from the back of the gullet is a near synonym for a husky one.

clue.text: Stationary motion and time study?

parts.note: reading is studying, as in reading for a degree

explanation.surface: A fitness routine involves standing still and taking time to study.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition calls to mind treading water, moving the legs while staying in one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading water involves constant leg movement without going anywhere, motion that is stationary.

clue.text: Speculation about limp could be 18

indicators.note: the word for speculation goes round the other

parts.note: a bet is a speculation, a wager
lank hair is limp

explanation.surface: Guessing about someone's limp might be thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed cover with heating wires inside it is a well-known warming appliance.

clue.text: Pick at food which doesn't appear completely thrilling

parts.note: to elect is to pick by vote

indicators.note: the food is not shown whole, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: Picking at one's dinner, which never quite appears, is hardly exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't appear completely' drops the last letter of RICE, leaving RIC. This is the theme word that many other clues point to.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciting atmosphere is often described as charged, as if with current, so this is a figurative synonym.

clue.text: The vessel in front could be 18

indicators.note: the vessel's word goes inside the word for front

parts.note: a face is a front, as the face of a building
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: The pot at the front might turn out to be thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is only a link; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial heating chamber can be powered by an electric arc, so this is an example of such a device.

clue.text: List of seafood cooked to a fine mush

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters have been worked over and mixed up

parts.note: the letters of fine mush

explanation.surface: Cooking turns the dish into a fine mush.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant card listing dishes from the sea.

clue.text: I don't "move in predestinate grooves" (Foot)

parts.note: taken as written
from a limerick whose speaker, moving in grooves, says he is not a bus but a tram; one who does not move in grooves can say 'am bus'

explanation.surface: Someone protests in quotation that they will not follow a fixed track, citing a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: A well-known limerick ends 'I'm an engine that moves in predestinate grooves; I'm not even a bus, I'm a tram'. A speaker who does not move in grooves is therefore a bus, not a tram.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of a short then a long syllable, also called an iamb.

clue.text: Facilitators of crime could be 18

definitions.meaning: receivers of stolen goods, who make theft pay
barriers round fields that can carry a shock

explanation.definitionFit: Receivers of stolen property make crime worthwhile, and farm barriers can be wired to deliver a shock.

clue.text: W.C. could be 18

definitions.meaning: in physics, regions around a charge where a force acts

explanation.walkthrough: W.C. looks like a lavatory, but it is the initials of the comedian W.C. Fields.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the comedian W.C., and in physics the regions of force around a charge.

clue.text: Losing one's head, as once following fiend with no manners

definitions.text: Losing one's head, as once following fiend with no manners

indicators.note: the beheaded word comes after the others

parts.note: an imp is a small fiend
rude means having no manners

indicators.note: the word once loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A warning that losing your head is rash, as when someone once followed an ill-mannered devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing one's head' cuts the first letter from ONCE, leaving NCE. The whole clue also describes rashness, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's head, acting rashly, is imprudence, and following a rude devil is just such rashness.

definitions.meaning: the lure that greyhounds chase round a track, driven along a rail

explanation.walkthrough: In British greyhound racing the dogs chase a mechanical lure called the hare, run round the track on a powered rail.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the dramatist David, and the powered lure greyhounds chase on a track.

clue.text: Bay as military award held by barbarian

indicators.note: the award sits inside the barbarian

parts.note: a Hun is a barbarian
DSO is the Distinguished Service Order

explanation.surface: A barbarian clutches a medal, as a bay horse might be described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' signals the container; 'as' is a link word.

clue.text: Sleuths who get Warbeck beheaded need a drink (with ice)

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, police detectives

indicators.note: the first letter of the name is removed

parts.note: Perkin Warbeck was a pretender to the English throne

explanation.walkthrough: Perkin Warbeck claimed the throne of Henry VII; 'beheaded' takes P from PERKIN to leave ERKIN. The parenthesis is decoration.
